01.actor: a woman selling belts and a man
01.event: a man snatches a belt from her; she demands it back
01.turn: he offers to return it as betrothal; she takes it and stays silent
01.outcome: Rav Nahman rules she can say she only took back her own property
01.summary: A woman was selling belts when a man snatched one from her. She demanded it back, and he asked whether, if he gave it, she would be betrothed to him. She took it and said nothing. Rav Nahman ruled that she could claim she merely took back what was hers.
01.reason: A narrated incident with more than one action (the snatching, her taking it back in silence), then a ruling: the R-C0 cow-case shape, not a bare case brought before a rabbi.

02.actor: the daughter-in-law of Nakdimon ben Guryon and the Sages
02.event: the Sages apportion her two se'a of wine a week for pudding
02.turn: she blesses them that they apportion so for their own daughters
02.outcome: they do not answer amen, since she was a widow awaiting her yavam
02.summary: The Sages apportioned the widowed daughter-in-law of Nakdimon ben Guryon two se'a of wine a week for cooking. She blessed them that they should apportion the same for their daughters. Because she was a widow waiting for her yavam, they did not answer amen.
02.reason: A courtroom apportionment that is itself an act, followed by speech and a pointed silence; the editor ruled this Ketubot 65a passage borderline as a little more than a ruling.

03.event: a divine anger (famine) in Rav Yosef's years; the Sages ask him to pray
03.outcome: he does not pray (implied by his answer)
03.summary: In Rav Yosef's years there was a famine. The Sages asked him to pray for mercy. He answered that if Elisha, who supported 2,200 Sages, did not pray in a time of anger, he should not either.
03.missing: any action or outcome beyond his spoken refusal
03.reason: There is a real event (the famine) but the passage is mainly a request and a spoken refusal; mainly speech with something happening is R-C7 shape 1, borderline.

04.event: betrothed a minor girl with a bundle of vegetables in the market
04.outcome: Ravina rules there is no concern the father desired it, as it was degrading
04.summary: A man betrothed a girl with a bundle of vegetables in the marketplace. Ravina ruled that because it was done in a degrading way, there is no concern the father desired it.
04.missing: any further action or change after the single act
04.reason: One event followed by a ruling and nothing changing afterwards; the editor ruled this shape not a story on 2026-10-25.

05.event: a man betrothed conditionally and then had relations
05.outcome: the Sages could not release her without a get
05.summary: Rav Kahana cites an incident in which a conditional betrothal was followed by intercourse, and the Sages lacked power to release the woman without a bill of divorce.
05.missing: the incident itself is only alluded to; no narrated actions or change
05.reason: An incident cited only as precedent for a ruling, a single implied act with no narrated change; R-C6 stops where what is told is one act with a ruling.

06.missing: any event beyond visiting and reciting a number of blessings
06.reason: Two reports of how many blessings a visitor recited at a wedding, cited as practice; a visit framing a halakhic data point is not a story.

07.actor: a certain person, Rav Yosef, Abaye
07.event: someone comes before Rav Yosef about a daughter's sustenance
07.turn: Rav Yosef rules from the dates; Abaye objects
07.outcome: Rav Yosef clarifies what he meant
07.summary: A person came before Rav Yosef, who ordered the heirs to sustain the daughter from dates on the mats. Abaye objected, and Rav Yosef explained he meant dates still fit for the mats.
07.missing: any narrated action or change beyond coming before the rabbi
07.reason: Coming before a rabbi is the only event, followed by a ruling and ordinary scholarly back-and-forth; R-C0's limit makes this not a story.

08.event: they come before Rav Yosef about her pregnancy
08.turn: she says it is from him
08.summary: A betrothed couple, the woman pregnant, came before Rav Yosef. She said the child was his, and he began to answer.
08.missing: his reply and the ruling fall in the context; no event beyond coming to court
08.reason: A case brought before a rabbi where coming before him is the only event, then claims and a ruling; not a story under R-C0's limit.

09.event: visits Neharde'a and sees a man tying a bolt with a reed
09.outcome: he rules the door may not be locked with it
09.summary: Rav Avya came to Neharde'a, saw a man tying a door bolt with a reed, and said it may not be used to lock the door.
09.missing: any response or change after the ruling
09.reason: A visit that only frames a ruling; the setting plus a ruling is not enough for a story (Shabbat 147a).

10.event: Rabbi Hanina regularly sends a pauper four dinars; one day he sends it with his wife
10.turn: she overhears that the pauper dines on silver or gold tablecloths and reports he does not need charity
10.outcome: Rabbi Hanina responds by citing Rabbi Elazar's saying in appreciation of swindlers
10.summary: Rabbi Hanina used to send a poor man four dinars every Shabbat eve. One day he sent them with his wife, who came back saying the man did not need charity, since she had heard his household asking whether he dined on silver or gold tablecloths. Rabbi Hanina answered with Rabbi Elazar's saying that we should be grateful to swindlers. The rest of the passage is legal discussion and a Mishna.
10.reason: A habitual frame followed by a one-time event, a discovery and a response: several actions and a change. Segments 4-18 are teaching, Mishna and sugya and are not part of the story.

11.event: the Sages send a reversed attribution to Rav Mordekhai
11.turn: he recalls Rav Ashi, one foot on the step, answering the question
11.outcome: the correct attribution: a child's gift is valid
11.summary: The Sages sent Rav Mordekhai the dispute with the names reversed. He sent back a reminder of how Rav Ashi, standing with one foot on the ground and one on the step, had told them a child's gift is valid.
11.missing: any event beyond sending messages and a remembered question and answer
11.reason: Transmission of a teaching: sending a question is a quasi-speech act and the recalled scene is a setting plus a question and answer, with no conflict beyond scholarly correction.

12.actor: an Amorite and a resident of Eretz Yisrael
12.event: the Amorite asks how much the Jordan palm yields
12.turn: he mocks that they have ruined the land; the resident retorts
12.outcome: the resident says he meant only one side of the tree
12.summary: An Amorite asked a man of Eretz Yisrael how much a palm by the Jordan yielded. Told sixty kor, he mocked that they had ruined the land, since his people took 120. The resident retorted that he was speaking of one side of the tree only.
12.reason: Pure dialogue with no event, but it has conflict (a taunt and a retort); speech with conflict is borderline under R-C2, as in the editor's ruling on Ketubot 112a.

13.event: Ravina visits Mehoza; his host shows him a slaughtering knife
13.outcome: Ravina tells him to take it to Rava
13.summary: Ravina came to Mehoza, and his host brought out a slaughtering knife and showed it to him. Ravina told him to take it to Rava.
13.missing: any change or consequence; the passage illustrates a ruling
13.reason: A visit that frames a halakhic question and a deferral, cited for the ruling that follows; a setting plus a question and answer is not a story.

14.event: Rava is silent before Rav Hamnuna's challenge
14.turn: after Hamnuna leaves he reasons out an answer, doubts it, then confirms it
14.outcome: he finds a baraita supporting the answer
14.summary: Faced with Rav Hamnuna's challenge, Rava fell silent. After Hamnuna left, Rava asked himself why he had not cited Rabbi Elazar, doubted the answer, and then confirmed it from a baraita.
14.missing: any event beyond silence and reasoning
14.reason: Raising and resolving a difficulty is speech, not an event; ordinary scholarly back-and-forth with no conflict beyond that.

15.actor: a certain man and Rav Nahman
15.event: a bachelor comes before Rav Nahman claiming he found an open orifice
15.outcome: Rav Nahman orders him flogged, inferring he has been with prostitutes
15.summary: A never-married man came before Rav Nahman and claimed his bride was not a virgin. Rav Nahman ordered him flogged, since he could only know this from prostitutes.
15.missing: whether the flogging happened; any change after the ruling
15.reason: A case brought before a rabbi and his ruling; the order only implies the outcome, which the editor ruled not a story on 2026-10-25.

16.missing: any event beyond a visit and a report of which blessings were recited
16.reason: A report of Rav Ashi's practice at a wedding, cited as halakhic precedent; nothing follows from it.

17.event: a man betrothed a woman within three months and fled
17.outcome: Rafram rules his flight is enough
17.summary: In an incident, a man betrothed a woman within three months of her divorce or widowhood and fled; Rafram ruled that his flight was penalty enough.
17.missing: the incident is only stated as a legal case; no further action or change
17.reason: An amoraic dispute followed by an incident alluded to only to report a ruling; one event then a ruling is not a story.

18.actor: a herdsman of orphans and a creditor
18.event: a creditor seizes an ox from the herdsman
18.turn: they dispute whether the seizure was before or after the debtor's death and come before Rav Nahman
18.outcome: Rav Nahman rules for the creditor since there are no witnesses to the seizure
18.summary: A creditor seized an ox from a herdsman tending orphans' cattle. They disputed whether he had seized it before or after the father's death and came before Rav Nahman, who asked about witnesses and, finding none, ruled the creditor could keep it.
18.reason: There is a narrated act besides the court appearance (the seizure), close to the R-C0 cow case, but it is essentially one event followed by a ruling; between borderline and not, borderline.

19.event: Me'oret made her slave perform three of the dangerous acts
19.summary: Within a legal discussion, the Gemara cites that a woman named Me'oret made her slave do three of the six dangerous acts and he died; it answers that the slave was weak.
19.missing: the incident is only alluded to as an objection, with no narrative detail
19.reason: A real incident with an act and a consequence, but only alluded to as evidence in the give-and-take; an alluded incident is borderline.

20.missing: any one-time event; only a habitual practice and its reason
20.reason: A report of Mareimar's practice of blocking Sura's alleys with nets, with his reasoning; a custom that leads nowhere is not a story.
